reason: In react-dom 19.3.1 the change only adds an isScriptDataBlock() exemption to the DEV-only console.error "Encountered a script tag while rendering React component" in react-dom-client.development.js (absent from the production build, and 19.1.0 has no such warning at all); the <script> element is created and rendered identically either way, so it is logging that application code cannot depend on.

In react-dom 19.3.1 the change is only a DEV-only console.error ("This library called use() to suspend in a previous render but did not call use() when it finished", recorded in trackUsedThenable and logged once on commit in react-dom-client.development.js, absent from the production build); rendering and suspension behave the same, so it is logging that application code cannot depend on.

Compared recoverFromConcurrentError in react-dom-client 19.1.0 and 19.3.1 (PR #36911: the error-recovery retry is no longer committed when it ends RootSuspendedAtTheShell; the population's "server-rendering" wording is off, it is the client's recovery render, e.g. while hydrating): the PR and its tests show the only observable effect of the old behavior is a later "Rendered more hooks than during the previous render" crash when a recovery render suspends on use() with no Suspense boundary, so code written for 19.1 is the same code as for 19.3 and only stops crashing, and no plausible application code depends on the old behavior.

In react-dom 19.3.1 the font wait lives only in the inline reveal script that react-dom/server streams to the browser (inside its document.startViewTransition branch it awaits document.fonts.ready and visible images, raced against a 500 ms to 2.3 s timer), so observing it needs a real browser's font loading and View Transitions, which jsdom lacks, and it would also be timing-dependent; nothing in react-dom/server's output or the client API differs for application code.

In react-dom 19.3.1 the shorthandToLonghand table is read only by the DEV-only console.error "Updating a style property during rerender ... when a conflicting property is set" in setValueForStyles (react-dom-client.development.js; the production build has no reference to it), and the styles applied to the DOM are the same, so the change only alters which combinations log a warning.

Confirmed in jsdom (a state update from a window resize listener: 19.1.0 renders it in the next microtask because resize had discrete priority, 19.3.1 renders it in a later scheduler task at continuous priority), but both settle to the same DOM before the next frame, so code written for 19.1 (resize listeners, useSyncExternalStore, layout effects) works unchanged and only code that reads the DOM in a microtask right after the event would notice, which no plausible application does and which would be timing-dependent to grade.
